senses.definition: One who sneaks; one who moves stealthily to acquire an item or information.
examples: My little brother is such a sneak; yesterday I caught him trying to look through my diary.
I can't believe I gave that sneak $50 for a ticket when they were selling for $20 at the front gate.

senses.definition: (obsolete, cricket) A ball bowled so as to roll along the ground; a daisy-cutter

quotes.text: We would have been laughed off the street in Philadelphia if we were seen wearing sneaks. In the big city, the young population wore loafers or boots.

senses.definition: (American football) A play where the quarterback receives the snap and immediately dives forward.

quotes.text: At a "sneak preview," of course, the public is also on hand and can make their reactions felt much to the humiliation of the principals. At a sneak of "The Sandpiper," starring Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, the audience laughed so loud during one love scene that the dejected producer promptly cut the scene out of the picture. At a sneak of "The Outrage" in San Francisco it was decided not to give names at the outset to test public response: nearly half the audience left before the picture was 20 minutes old. […] The worst sneak, it is told, occurred one night when nearly the entire audience marched out on "Paris When It Sizzles” leaving the producer and director alone and forlorn in the theater.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To creep or go stealthily; to come or go while trying to avoid detection, as a person who does not wish to be seen.
examples: He decided to sneak into the kitchen for a second cookie while his mom was on the phone.

quotes.text: Some of these were dressed most gorgeously, others becomingly, and several sneaked in with fantail bangers, calling themselves "Gentlemen of the Nineteenth Century."

senses.definition: (transitive) To take something stealthily without permission.
examples: I went to sneak a chocolate but my dad caught me.
She asked me to sneak her a phone next month.

senses.definition: (transitive, dated) To hide, especially in a mean or cowardly manner.

quotes.reference: 1701, William Wake, A rationale upon some texts of Scripture:

senses.definition: (intransitive, informal, with on) To inform an authority of another's misdemeanours.
examples: If you sneak on me I'll bash you!

senses.definition: In advance; before release to the general public.
examples: The company gave us a sneak look at their new electronic devices.

senses.definition: In a stealthy or surreptitious manner.
examples: I was able to get a sneak peek at the guest list.

quotes.text: I have ordered House Atreides to occupy Arrakis to mine the spice, thus replacing their enemies the Harkonnens. House Atreides will not refuse because of the tremendous power they think they will gain. Then, at an appointed time, Baron Harkonnen will return to Arrakis and launch a sneak attack on House Atreides. I have promised the Baron five legions of my Sardaukar terror troops.
